items.title: [Recipe] add FLUX.2-klein-4B L40S recipe
items.body: ## Purpose Add a community recipe for `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B`, personally validated for offline text-to-image generation on 1x NVIDIA L40S 48 GB. The recipe documents: - the exact hardware and software environment; - the shared offline text-to-image runner command; - BF16, TP=1, 1024x1024, four-step generation settings; - model-level CPU offload and VAE tiling; - output integrity and visual verification; - generation latency, initialization time, and peak VRAM; and - assumptions, measurement methodology, and unvalidated configurations. It also adds the recipe to `recipes/README.md`. Related to #2645. Claim: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/2645#issuecomment-5348334920 ## Test Plan Personally validated end to end on one NVIDIA L40S 48 GB using the shared offline text-to-image runner: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python3 examples/offline_inference/text_to_image/text_to_image.py \ --model black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B \ --prompt "A red fox wearing round blue glasses holds a white sign that clearly reads 'vLLM-Omni L40S', studio photograph, plain gray background." \ --seed 0 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --num-images-per-prompt 1 \ --num-inference-steps 4 \ --guidance-scale 1.0 \ --height 1024 \ --width 1024 \ --enable-cpu-offload \ --vae-use-tiling \ --output flux2-klein-4b-l40s.png ``` Documentation checks: ```text git diff --check Passed fix end of files Passed mixed line ending Passed trim trailing whitespace Passed typos Passed markdownlint-cli2 Passed ``` **vLLM Version:** `0.27.1` **vLLM-Omni Commit:** `2fdbf2234` (`0.27.0rc2.dev78+g2fdbf2234`) ## Test Result Environment: ```text GPU: 1x NVIDIA L40S, 46,068 MiB NVIDIA driver: 580.173.02 CUDA reported by nvidia-smi: 13.0 Python: 3.12.14 PyTorch: 2.13.0 Diffusers: 0.38.0 Transformers: 5.14.1 ``` Runner result: ```text Model-level offloading enabled: transformer <-> text_encoder (mutual exclusion) Processed prompts: 100%|██████████| 1/1 [00:13<00:00, 13.32s/it] Total generation time: 13.3234 seconds (13323.44 ms) Saved generated image to flux2-klein-4b-l40s.png ``` Measurements: ```text Runner exit status: 0 Generation latency: 13.3234 seconds Denoising latency per step: 3.330 seconds Engine initialization: 55.48 seconds Initial model download: 32.93 seconds Full cold-process wall time: 133.38 seconds Worker-reported peak GPU memory: 12,110 MB Sampled device-wide peak GPU memory: 12,707 MiB (12.409 GiB) ``` Output verification: ```text format=PNG size=1024x1024 mode=RGB bytes=1260085 rgb_mean=169.539,160.801,157.142 rgb_extrema=((0, 255), (0, 255), (0, 255)) sha256=bb88fb56547ad342e4df1e1a07f6bebd299afb5c6f25b55f19f66e8fe38ce4d4 ``` Visual inspection confirmed the requested red fox, round blue glasses, white sign, `vLLM-Omni L40S` text, and plain gray background. No obvious VAE tile-boundary seams were visible. ### Generated output

items.title: docs: add Qwen-Image-Layered L40S recipe
items.body:
## Purpose

Add a community recipe for running `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Layered` on a single
NVIDIA L40S 48 GB GPU using layer-wise CPU offloading.

The recipe documents a personally validated offline inference configuration for
layered image decomposition at 640 resolution with four RGBA output layers.

Related to #2645.

## Changes

Adds:

- `recipes/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Layered.md`

The recipe documents:

- tested L40S hardware and software environment
- exact offline inference command
- layer-wise CPU offloading configuration
- end-to-end validation
- observed generation latency and GPU memory usage
- known CFG behavior for the validated command

## Environment

- GPU: 1x NVIDIA L40S
- Available GPU memory: 46,068 MiB
- Host RAM: 124 GiB
- NVIDIA driver: 580.173.02
- Python: 3.12.14
- CUDA: 13.0
- PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130`
- vLLM: `0.27.1`
- vLLM-Omni: `0.27.0rc2.dev78+g2fdbf2234`
- vLLM-Omni commit: `2fdbf2234aeb76715618a5b236f0016f115e3e64`

## Test Plan

Personally validated the recipe end-to-end using the existing generic
image-to-image example:

```bash
python examples/offline_inference/image_to_image/image_edit.py \
  --model "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Layered" \
  --image qwen-bear.png \
  --prompt "" \
  --output "layered_50" \
  --num-inference-steps 50 \
  --cfg-scale 4.0 \
  --layers 4 \
  --resolution 640 \
  --color-format RGBA \
  --enable-layerwise-offload
```

Validated that:

- the model loads successfully on 1x NVIDIA L40S 48 GB
- layer-wise offloading is enabled across the transformer blocks
- all 50 inference steps complete without OOM
- four output layers are generated successfully
- all four generated layers were manually inspected and contained meaningful layered image content
- GPU memory remains stable during the main denoising loop

GPU memory was sampled at one-second intervals using `nvidia-smi`.

## Test Results

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Inference steps | 50/50 |
| Output layers | 4 |
| Resolution | 640 |
| Color format | RGBA |
| Layer-wise offload | Enabled |
| Total generation time | 155.97 s |
| Denoising loop | ~150 s |
| Average denoising step | ~3.00 s |
| GPU memory after model loading | ~17.17 GiB |
| Peak observed GPU memory | 26,863 MiB (~26.23 GiB) |

Generated outputs:

```text
layered_50_0.png
layered_50_1.png
layered_50_2.png
layered_50_3.png
```

During the main denoising phase, GPU utilization remained approximately
99-100%, while observed GPU memory stayed stable at about 26,863 MiB.

The runtime reported layer-wise offloading across 60
`QwenImageTransformerBlock` instances.

## Notes

- `--enable-layerwise-offload` offloads transformer blocks between host memory
  and GPU memory to reduce GPU memory requirements.
- The validation used tensor parallel size 1 and no distributed execution.
- The machine had 124 GiB of host RAM.
- `--cfg-scale 4.0` was supplied during validation. The pipeline reported that
  true classifier-free guidance was not enabled because no negative prompt was
  provided. The recipe documents this behavior explicitly rather than claiming
  that CFG was active.

## Summary

Adds a community recipe for running `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo` with vLLM-Omni for text-to-image generation.

The recipe includes:
- validated environment and hardware setup
- Hugging Face cache setup for large model downloads
- offline inference example

items.body:
## Purpose

Adds a ROCm recipe for DreamZero-DROID. `recipes/` currently covers one robot policy, GR00T-N1.7, CUDA only.

Two things about the published ROCm images, both recorded in the recipe's Notes:

- v0.24.0 and v0.24.1 cannot serve DreamZero — their   `dreamzero_tp1_cfg2.yaml` is missing `engine_backend`, added in #5439, but not in a published ROCM image yet. here still with **v0.22.0**
- 
- **v0.22.0 needs `pip install openpi-client` on the server**, which the image  does not ship. The failure looks like a client-side `ConnectionClosedError`,  so the note points at the server log. Not needed after v0.22.0.

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.22.0+rocm722

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** base `d77a35a3`; the documented configuration is tag `v0.22.0`

2x AMD MI300X (gfx942), ROCm/HIP 7.2.53211, Ubuntu 22.04.5, Python 3.12, torch 2.10.0+git8514f05, image
`vllm/vllm-omni-rocm:v0.22.0@sha256:be06edae7ba9d14a89c5907da2e3631b7998765bce285c937f7d9a96e6aeb2c5`.

On a clean `v0.22.0` checkout with the published image — no locally built image, no out-of-tree patches:

1. The e2e test:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
    tests/e2e/online_serving/test_dreamzero_expansion.py::test_dreamzero_openpi_online
```

2. The recipe's `vllm serve` command, driven by the in-tree example client
   `examples/online_serving/dreamzero/openpi_client.py`.

## Test Result

```
1 passed, 17 warnings in 184.01s (0:03:04)
```

```
Server metadata: {"action_space": "joint_position", "image_resolution": [180, 320],
                  "n_external_cameras": 2, "needs_session_id": true,
                  "needs_stereo_camera": false, "needs_wrist_camera": true}
Action 0: shape=(24, 8) dtype=float32 min=-0.120401 max=0.540639
Action 1: shape=(24, 8) dtype=float32 min=-0.003906 max=0.421654
```

Weights load at 42.79 GiB per rank.

## Not in scope

- **No latency numbers.** Functional validation only.
- **Single session.** `max_num_seqs: 1`; stated as a limitation, not tested.
- **ROCm section only**, leaving the CUDA section to whoever validates it.
- **Not validated against `main`.** v0.22.0 is the newest ROCm image published.
  Re-pin when a newer one ships; that also retires both notes above.

items.title: [Recipe] MiniMax-H3 on A100-SXM4-40GB (TP4 + CPU offload / DLO)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a deployment recipe for MiniMax-H3 on **NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB** (sm80), the
missing datacenter row in the hardware matrix (4090/5090/PRO 5000/6000/H20/DGX-Spark exist; A100 does not).

Two paths are documented, both validated end-to-end on this node (official 1344×768 reference video with audio, 480×256/96 frames, seed 0):

| Path | Per-GPU HBM (nvidia-smi) | End-to-end inference time | API worker-aggregated peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 + CPU offload | ~22.3 GiB peak (reference-KV cache active) | 364.5 s | 32,098 MB |
| DLO rank-local (TP1 + DP4, shared-mmap) | ~12.4 GiB peak (12,583–12,685 MiB) | 2012.8 s | 19,108 MB |

Key constraints documented:
- **sm80 → BF16 only**: NVFP4 and hardware FP8 are unavailable on A100 (FP8 tensor cores need sm89+).
- Model-level CPU offload via `--enable-cpu-offload` (sequential offload) is the primary path; the
  vLLM-core offload flags (`--cpu-offload-gb`, `--offload-group-size`, ...) from the 4×L40S report are
  no-ops for diffusion and were removed from the command. DLO rank-local (official TP1 shared-mmap
  topology, #6213) is the lower-HBM alternative.

Also links the new recipe from the main MiniMax-H3 recipe.

## Test Plan

- Validated on a node with 8×A100-SXM4-40GB, using **4 of the 8 GPUs** for each command
  (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3`; a co-tenant occupied another GPU, so TP8 was not exercised — the
  "Eight A100-40GB" section is explicitly marked as an estimate).
- Both paths: end-to-end Ref2VA generation completed (`status=completed`, progress 100, valid h264
  480×256 MP4 with AAC audio); peak HBM measured live with nvidia-smi during the runs using the
  official reference video (see the validation comments on this PR).
- The vLLM-Omni pipeline resolves the partition directory (FL2VA/Ref2VA) automatically;
  weights load from Hugging Face (MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) or ModelScope (MiniMax/MiniMax-H3).

items.title: Add measured 8x H200 numbers to the Cosmos3-Super recipe
items.body:
## Purpose

### Add measured 8x H200 numbers to the Cosmos3-Super recipe

The recipe documents the 8x H200/H100/A100 command and carries measured latencies for
2x B300, but the 8-GPU cell has only NVIDIA's quoted reference figure. This adds
measurements taken with the documented 8-GPU command, using the same methodology as the
existing 2x B300 entry: bf16, official generation parameters
(`size=1280x720, num_frames=189, fps=24, guidance_scale=6.0, flow_shift=10.0,
max_sequence_length=4096`), prompt and negative prompt from the model repo's own
`assets/`, guardrails off unless stated.

Headline numbers, all server-side `stage_gen_time_ms`, n=3 unless noted: the
documented CFG-parallel 2 x Ulysses 4 x HSDP 8 config runs the 35-step shape in
~121 s and 50 steps in ~166 s (the 50-step figure is server-side n=1 with wall
times at n=3). A same-host `--tensor-parallel-size 8` control at identical shape
and seed runs ~131 s and ~181 s, so TP-8 is about 9% slower than the documented
config on this hardware. Every cell fits a simple decomposition,
latency ~= 14.4 s + steps x per-step, within 0.3%: the two strategies differ only in
denoise-step rate (3.03-3.06 vs 3.33-3.36 s/step), and the ~14.4 s remainder is
invariant. Three further strategies (Ulysses+Ring hybrid, Ulysses-8 without CFG
parallelism, VAE patch parallelism added to the documented config) measured slower
or neutral, so the documented config was the fastest of the five tried.

Guardrails add ~18 s (+15%) on the model repo's upsampled example prompt but only
~2 s on randomized prompts at the same shape, so the entry states guardrail cost as
prompt-dependent. Determinism gets one caveat the recipe does not currently carry:
output is bitwise reproducible at a fixed seed within one server instance, but a
server restart changes the output at the same seed (median PSNR 28 dB against the
pre-restart clip, comparable to adjacent-frame difference), so same-seed
comparisons are only valid within one instance.

The second change is a note that enabling guardrails on this image currently needs
`HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1`. Once the token has guardrail access, startup still fails inside
`huggingface_hub`'s xet path with `Unable to parse string as hex hash value`. That is
huggingface/xet-core#895, which reproduces on the exact pair this image pins, hf-xet
1.5.1 and huggingface_hub 1.23.0, and which closed on 2026-07-28, eight days after the
image was pushed. Disabling xet downloads the guardrail repo in under two minutes and
the server comes up clean. Bumping those two pins in the image would remove the need for
the env var, though I have not tested a bumped image.

One note on the reference figures the doc quotes. The model card's ~55 s claim
specifies 50 steps and H200 but no frame count; at 189 frames, 50 steps measured
~166 s here, and ~55 s would need a per-step rate ~3.7x faster than anything
measured, so it most plausibly describes a shorter clip. The 111.94 s in
`inference_benchmarks.md` is a tensor-parallel figure per its methodology note and
states no step count; at the TP-8 per-step rate measured here it corresponds to
roughly 29-30 steps. Both readings would explain the published numbers without
either measurement being wrong, and I am happy to be told the measurement is
missing something.

Happy to add I2V, T2V with sound, or additional step counts if those would be
useful in the same block.

Hardware: 8x H200 SXM 141 GB, NVLink full mesh, driver 580.126.09, on Nebius AI Cloud.
Full logs and the generated clips are available on request.

## Test Plan

Documentation-only change to `recipes/cosmos3/Cosmos3-Super.md`; no code paths are
touched. The hardware, generation parameters, methodology, and repetition counts behind
every number are stated in full under Purpose and in the added recipe block itself.

**vLLM Version:** 0.25.0

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** 0.25.0rc2.dev62+g9c1b7504b (image `vllm/vllm-omni:cosmos3`, `sha256:6d2630c7d637...`)

## Test Result

The measured values being added are listed under Purpose. The diff adds one bullet block
to the `#### Notes` section under the GPU heading, immediately after the existing
2x B300 measured block, and changes nothing else.

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Add a new community recipe for serving `k2-fsa/OmniVoice` with vLLM-Omni on `1x NVIDIA L20 48GB`.

The recipe documents the tested online serving path for multilingual TTS through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` API.

Contributes to #2645.

## Test Plan

This is a documentation-only recipe PR. No model code, tests, dependencies, or serving behavior are changed.

The documented serving smoke tests were run on `1x NVIDIA L20 48GB`.

Tested commands and checks:

- Downloaded `k2-fsa/OmniVoice`.
- Started online serving with:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve k2-fsa/OmniVoice \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8091 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --omni
```

- Checked the health endpoint:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8091/health
```

- Sent an English TTS request:

```bash
python examples/online_serving/omnivoice/speech_client.py \
  --api-base http://127.0.0.1:8091 \
  --model k2-fsa/OmniVoice \
  --text "Hello, this is an OmniVoice smoke test on one NVIDIA L20 GPU." \
  --output omnivoice_l20_en.wav
```

- Sent a Chinese TTS request:

```bash
python examples/online_serving/omnivoice/speech_client.py \
  --api-base http://127.0.0.1:8091 \
  --model k2-fsa/OmniVoice \
  --text "你好，这是一个 OmniVoice 的中文语音合成测试。" \
  --language Chinese \
  --output omnivoice_l20_zh.wav
```

- Sent a raw `/v1/audio/speech` request:

```bash
curl -sS \
  -w "\nhttp_code=%{http_code}\nsize_download=%{size_download}\ntime_total=%{time_total}\n" \
  -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8091/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "k2-fsa/OmniVoice",
    "input": "This is a raw curl smoke test for OmniVoice on one NVIDIA L20 GPU.",
    "voice": "default",
    "response_format": "wav"
  }' \
  --output omnivoice_l20_curl.wav
```

- Validated that generated WAV files were non-empty and readable.

No unit tests were run because this PR only adds documentation. The serving smoke tests above validate the documented recipe.

## Test Result

Environment:

- GPU: `1x NVIDIA L20 48GB`
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Driver: `580.126.09`
- CUDA: `13.0`
- Python: `3.12.13`
- PyTorch: `2.10.0+cu130`
- vLLM: `0.19.0`
- vLLM-Omni commit: `dd0fa02547aae9f57e1cb1c80b7db50a4161b8d2`
- Transformers: `4.57.6`

Health check:

```text
Server is healthy after 35 seconds.
```

Raw `/v1/audio/speech` request:

```text
http_code=200
size_download=203564
time_total=0.659745
```

Audio validation:

```text
omnivoice_l20_en.wav:
  size_bytes: 190124
  channels: 1
  sample_width: 2
  sample_rate: 24000
  frames: 95040
  duration_sec: 3.96

omnivoice_l20_zh.wav:
  size_bytes: 188204
  channels: 1
  sample_width: 2
  sample_rate: 24000
  frames: 94080
  duration_sec: 3.92

omnivoice_l20_curl.wav:
  size_bytes: 203564
  channels: 1
  sample_width: 2
  sample_rate: 24000
  frames: 101760
  duration_sec: 4.24
```

Final GPU status showed `3660 MiB / 46068 MiB` GPU memory in use on NVIDIA L20.

Notes:

- This is a documentation-only change.
- Voice cloning and voice design are not covered by this smoke test.
- No model code, tests, dependencies, or serving behavior are changed.

items.title: [Recipe] Tongyi/Z-Image-Turbo (RTX 5090 32GB)
items.body:
## Summary

Add a new community recipe for serving `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo` on `1x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 32GB`.

This recipe documents:
- environment details for an AutoDL-based CUDA setup
- online serving with the OpenAI-compatible image generation API
- a no-`jq` verification path using `response_format: "file"`
- validated server-side and client-side output checks

## Related Issue

- related to #2645

## Environment

- OS: Linux (AutoDL container)
- Python: `3.12.3`
- PyTorch: `2.7.0+cu128`
- Driver: `580.105.08`
- CUDA runtime: `13.0`
- GPU: `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 32GB`
- vLLM-Omni commit: `86bdcaf3`

## Test Plan

1. Start the server:

```bash
export HF_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/hf
export HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE=/root/autodl-tmp/hf/hub
export TRANSFORMERS_CACHE=/root/autodl-tmp/hf/transformers
export TORCH_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/torch
export TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/root/autodl-tmp/triton
export TMPDIR=/root/autodl-tmp/tmp

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo \
  --omni \
  --port 8000
```

2. Check health:

```bash
curl -s -o /tmp/zimage_health.txt -w '%{http_code}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

3. Send an online generation request without `jq`:

```bash
curl -o /tmp/z_image_turbo_5090.png \
  -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "a cup of coffee on the table",
    "size": "1024x1024",
    "num_inference_steps": 9,
    "guidance_scale": 0.0,
    "seed": 42,
    "response_format": "file"
  }'
```

4. Verify the saved file:

```bash
ls -lh /tmp/z_image_turbo_5090.png
file /tmp/z_image_turbo_5090.png
```

## Test Results

- Server returned `HTTP 200 OK` for `/v1/images/generations`
- Request parameters:
  - resolution: `1024x1024`
  - batch size: `1`
  - `num_inference_steps=9`
  - `guidance_scale=0.0`
  - `seed=42`
- Server-side observed metrics:
  - `e2e_wall_time_ms = 5125.196`
  - `e2e_avg_time_per_request_ms = 5125.196`
  - `e2e_stage_0_wall_time_ms = 5120.172`
  - `denoise_step_latency_ms = 568.803`
  - `serving_time_to_first_output_ms = 5124.620`
- Client-side observed output:
  - file path: `/tmp/z_image_turbo_5090.png`
  - file size: `3.1M`
  - file type: `PNG image data, 1024 x 1024, 8-bit/color RGB, non-interlaced`
- Observed GPU memory footprint during model load / serving: about `24.8 GiB`

## Notes

- `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo` is a distilled diffusion model, so this recipe uses `4-9` steps and `guidance_scale=0.0` instead of a Qwen-Image-style 50-step CFG setup.
- The verification path intentionally avoids `jq`, since `response_format: "file"` works better in minimal environments.

items.body:
## Summary

- Add a Cosmos3-Nano low-VRAM online serving recipe validated on 1x RTX 5090 32GB.
- Document the BF16 launch command with `--enable-layerwise-offload`, `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`, and CUDNN attention.
- Add reduced-size validation results for T2I and T2V, including latency, peak GPU memory, and output validation.

Related to #4340

## Duplicate-work check

This does not duplicate an existing open PR.

Checked:
- `gh api 'repos/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/4340/comments?per_page=100'`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm-omni --state open --search "4340 in:body"`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm-omni --state open --search "Cosmos3 Nano RTX 5090 low VRAM recipe"`

Existing open PRs mentioning #4340 are for Cosmos3 L2/L3 tests, pipeline parallel, and TeaCache, not this RTX 5090 low-VRAM recipe.

## Validation

Runtime validation was performed on 1x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 32GB with Cosmos3-Nano.

- Without `--enable-layerwise-offload`, BF16 startup loaded the model but failed the startup dummy run with CUDA OOM after using 31.09 GiB.
- With `--enable-layerwise-offload`, T2I 512x512, 20 steps completed in 9.72s with peak GPU memory 19931 MiB.
- With `--enable-layerwise-offload`, T2V 512x512, 33 frames, 20 steps completed in 11.74s with peak GPU memory 23241 MiB.
- T2I output decoded as 512x512 RGB PNG.
- T2V output decoded as H.264 MP4, 512x512, 24 fps, 33 frames.

This validates the reduced-size low-VRAM deployment path. Full 720p / 189-frame validation and other modalities remain out of scope for this PR.

- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`
- `file /tmp/cosmos3_rtx5090_validation/cosmos3_rtx5090_t2i_512.png /tmp/cosmos3_rtx5090_validation/cosmos3_rtx5090_t2v_512_33f.mp4`

items.title: [Doc] Add recipe for Cosmos3 video generation pinned to start and end boundaries
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
Add an inference-only Cosmos3 recipe and client for generating a video pinned to start and end boundaries (frame or short clip), with the middle filled from an event prompt (FL2V).

## Purpose

Stock Cosmos3 V2V locks a clean prefix of latents (typically `[0, 1]`). This PR documents and ships a client path that locks a contiguous latent range at **both** ends via existing request fields (`condition_frame_indexes_vision` + a clean head/tail reference video). No vLLM-Omni source or weight changes.

Includes:
- `recipes/cosmos3/Cosmos3-FL2V.md` — setup, serve/run, how it works, troubleshooting
- `tools/cosmos3_fl2v/` — HTTP client, required SHM patch for large FL2V payloads, demo seeds/prompts
- `.gitignore` allow-list for the demo prompt JSON files

Prefer `nvidia/Cosmos3-Super` for quality; `nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano` also works on the same client (verified).

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.26.0

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** this PR branch (`add-cosmos3-fl2v`)

- Apply `tools/cosmos3_fl2v/patch_vllm_shm.py` in the server env
- Serve `nvidia/Cosmos3-Super` (or Nano) with `vllm serve … --omni`
- Run `python fl2v_generate_vllm.py --dry-run` (client-only sanity)
- Run frame+frame demo against a warm server; confirm start/end PSNR and output MP4

## Test Result

- Dry-run: `latent_frames=48`, conditioning latents `[0, 47]`, reference frames `189`
- Nano on H100 and Super on B200/H200: generation completed; boundaries pinned
- Without the SHM patch, large FL2V payloads hang silently (as documented)

items.title: [CI][Bugfix] Align the LTX-2 FP8 quality gate with the default recipe
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->


## Purpose

Fixes [#5733](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5733).

The old `fp8_ltx2` case pinned a pre-#5148 custom sigma trajectory. The current LTX pipeline intentionally uses the official multimodal guidance recipe, so this mixed old scheduling with new guidance and exceeded the historical LPIPS threshold.

The gate now measures the supported eager default recipe:

- Lightricks/LTX-2 online FP8 versus BF16;
- `512x384`, 73 frames, 10 steps, seed 42;
- no request sigma or guidance override;
- recipe-default negative conditioning;
- `enforce_eager=True` for both runs, so compile behavior is not part of a
  quantization-quality assertion.

The LPIPS threshold follows the standard video quality gate at `0.20`; this PR does not change quantization implementation.

## Test Result

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/diffusion/quantization/test_quantization_quality.py \
  -m '' -k 'test_quantization_quality and fp8_ltx2' -s
```

| Metric | Result | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---:|
| LPIPS | 0.0418 | <= 0.20 |
| PSNR | 33.0941 dB | Reported |
| MAE | 0.017016 | Reported |

The small configuration tests and changed-file pre-commit hooks also pass.

items.title: [Doc][Model] Add validated low-VRAM Cosmos3-Nano recipe for 16GB Ada GPUs
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds a documentation-only low-VRAM T2I recipe for serving
`nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano` on a single RTX 4080 Super 16GB through vLLM-Omni.

The recipe is intentionally scoped to:

- T2I only (`/v1/images/generations`)
- RTX 4080 Super 16GB
- WSL2 host with `memory=24GB` and `swap=8GB`
- no guardrails

It does not claim that T2V/I2V/V2V/audio/action modes are validated on this
hardware.

## Evidence

Validation run: `LV150`

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Server ready time | 414.9 s |
| T2I request latency | 19.77 s |
| Startup peak VRAM | 15.62 GiB |
| Startup WSL RAM | 19.55 GiB |
| Response | HTTP 200, valid 1024x1024 RGB PNG |

The run used the exact recipe now documented, selected
`TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` automatically, and completed a 1024x1024 T2I
request without PR #5013 or a forced Marlin test environment variable.

## Why These Knobs Are Included

- `--enable-layerwise-offload` keeps the model viable on 16GB VRAM.
- `--quantization fp8_per_block` uses vLLM's online FP8 per-block shorthand.
- `--disable-multithread-weight-load` limits concurrent host allocations while
  loading shards in the constrained WSL2 memory envelope.
- `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1` avoids an observed Torch Dynamo/Inductor compile
  failure in the online FP8 cast path.
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.60` leaves enough startup and request headroom.

## Dependency

This PR intentionally remains in Draft until #5021 is merged. That bugfix
restores construction of vLLM's online quantization shorthands on current main.
After #5021 merges, this branch will be updated to merged main and the documented
command will receive a final smoke validation before this PR is marked ready.

## Tests

Documentation-only change.

Runtime validation:

```text
LV150: server_start_success=true, response_success=true,
startup_peak_vram_gb=15.6240234375,
startup_wsl_ram_gb=19.54561996459961,
end_to_end_latency_s=19.77016969997203
```

Documentation checks:

```text
git diff --check
uvx pre-commit run --files recipes/cosmos3/Cosmos3-Nano.md
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. The saved output was independently
opened as a 1024x1024 RGB PNG.

## Scope Control

This PR is docs-only and intentionally avoids bundling implementation changes.
The runtime fix remains isolated in #5021. Output quality and prompt following
are outside this recipe's runtime-validation claim.

items.title: [Docs] Add recipe for Qwen-Image-Layered on 2x 48GB GPUs
items.body:
## Summary

Add a community recipe for running `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Layered` on two 48 GB GPUs when a single large-memory GPU (e.g., 80 GB A100) is not available.

Follows the suggestion from @hsliuustc0106 in #2905.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `recipes/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Layered.md` | New recipe: environment, command, verification, and performance notes |
| `recipes/README.md` | Add index entry for the new recipe |

## Tested Configuration

- **Hardware**: 2\u00d7 NVIDIA RTX 5880-Ada-48Q (48 GB each)
- **Key flags**: `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-cpu-offload`
- **Results**: Model loads at ~15.7 GiB/GPU, peak ~34.2 GB/GPU, generation completes in ~65s
- **Output**: Two correct RGBA PNG layers (480\u00d7864) from a 720\u00d71280 input image

## Motivation

The model weights (~45 GB) exceed single 48 GB card capacity. This recipe documents a working multi-GPU configuration using tensor parallelism and CPU offloading, validated on real hardware.
